subject: CrestonAI - Dedicated reservation options and phased ramp proposal
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@crestonai.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Moss <elena.moss@crestonai.com>, procurement@crestonai.com
Date: 2028-05-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — high-level numbers

David — thanks for the chat this morning. As mentioned, our immediate goal is a predictable inference baseline for our flagship product (real-time summaries + multimodal retrieval) with burst capacity for nightly batch jobs. A few clarifying questions before we take a proposal to procurement: 

- Minimum steady-state GPUs you recommend for 99th-pct latency < 250ms for 1k concurrent streams?
- Can we structure a short pilot (4 weeks) at smaller capacity with a guaranteed smooth ramp to full commit?
- Any network/NIC constraints for private VPC deployment we should flag to infra?

Appreciate a concise plan we can hand to procurement.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Infrastructure, CrestonAI
[phone redacted]
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@crestonai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — high-level numbers

Sanjay — thanks, quick reply with a recommended starting construct and ramp. Attaching a one-page offer and a tentative onboarding timeline. Key bullets: 

- Pilot: 10 GPUs (A100-80GB equivalent) for 4 weeks to validate latency and KV-cache hit patterns; includes 1 warm standby node for failover.
- Minimum steady-state: 30 GPUs to sustain 1k concurrent low-latency streams with 99th-pct < 250ms given typical request sizes (avg. seq_len 512) and model quantization to int8.
- Full committed band / production target: 80 GPUs across 2 AZs for throughput and fault tolerance.
- Ramp schedule: 10 (pilot) -> 30 (week 3 post-pilot) -> 50 (week 7) -> 80 (week 12). Each step is gated by SLA and perf evals.
- Warm pool / burst lanes: we suggest enabling a 15% warm standby buffer and ability to burst to +20% using shared spare capacity for scheduled nightly batches.
- Networking: 25 Gbps per host recommended; we’ll provide a firewall/VPC template and peering checklist.

If procurement needs alternate billing phasing (quarterly commit tranches) we can draft a tranche schedule and credits for pilot. Attaching files.

Regards,
David
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: creston_dedicated_offer_v1.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: mvp-onboarding-timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Elena Moss <elena.moss@crestonai.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@crestonai.com>
Cc: procurement@crestonai.com
Date: 2028-05-05T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — high-level numbers

David — this looks promising. A couple of procurement-specific asks from our side: 

1) Can you split the commitment into 2-year with an option to scale up in year 2 at pre-agreed rates?
2) We need a minimum-guarantee clause on capacity and a fall-forward policy if you have transient shortages.
3) Any volume discounts or startup credits to offset pilot costs?

Also looping in our procurement lead (procurement@crestonai.com) to coordinate terms. We’ll review the offer and timeline then come back with internal questions.

—Elena
Director, Product Ops, CrestonAI
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moss <elena.moss@crestonai.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@crestonai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-06T10:54:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — high-level numbers

Elena — great questions. Short answers so procurement can move fast: 

1) 2-year commitment: yes; we can lock a baseline rate for year 1 and provide a structured scale-up discount band for year 2 (3x tier breakpoints). We’ll include an escalation cap.
2) Minimum-guarantee clause: we propose a minimum-available GPU baseline equal to 90% of committed steady-state with automatic crediting for any sustained shortfall > 1 hour. For transient regional shortages we offer automated model fallback to compatible instance types (documented comp table) and a crediting SLA.
3) Pilot credits: we can apply a one-time credit equal to 25% of the pilot invoice toward the first tranche if you sign within 30 days of pilot completion.

Operational notes: onboarding cadence assumes instrumentation of 3 benchmark prompt sets and an SRE workshop week to configure KV cache warmups and batching profiles. Karthik — can you confirm the warm-pool sizing recommendation (15% vs 20%) and note any additional prewarm actions?

-David
[Attachment: network-reqs.txt (text)]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Elena Moss <elena.moss@crestonai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@crestonai.com>
Date: 2028-05-08T15:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — high-level numbers

Elena / Sanjay — quick technical confirmation from infra/serving side: 

- Warm-pool guidance: 15% warm pool for steady-state plus a single pre-warmed hot-standby host per AZ. This balances cost and turn-up latency; if you expect frequent 2x spikes we recommend 20%.
- Prewarm actions: KV cache seeding for top-100 prompt prefixes, persistent optimizer warm starts on service start, and a rolling-canary deployment for model variants during ramp.
- Minimum GPU sizing: 30 GPUs is the safe minimum for your SLA target given current perf tests; we can reduce to 25 only if you accept a higher 99th-pct tail in exchange for cost savings.

Next steps: if procurement confirms tranche preference I’ll update the onboarding workbook with exact activation windows and runbook triggers.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
